title: Sell Mineral Rights in Prichard, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Prichard, AL | Mobile County
metaDescription: Hold mineral rights tied to Prichard, AL family land? Get a courthouse-verified, no-pressure offer from a direct buyer.
heroLead: Prichard grew up alongside Mobile as a working port and rail community, and mineral interests connected to families here often trace back to farmland the family held before the area urbanized in the twentieth century.
intro: As Prichard developed, a lot of the surrounding farmland was sold off in pieces for housing and industry, and mineral rights sometimes traveled with those sales and sometimes didn't, depending on how each individual deed was written. What we see most often from Prichard families is an inherited interest connected to a rural relative's land elsewhere in Mobile County — the family's roots are in Prichard, but the actual mineral acreage sits somewhere out toward Citronelle or the county's western edge.

sections.heading: Urban Roots, Rural Mineral Interest
paragraphs: If your family has lived in Prichard for generations but holds a mineral interest connected to a grandparent's farm elsewhere in the county, the two are treated separately in the title record. We locate and confirm the actual mineral tract regardless of where the family lives today.

sections.heading: Older Deeds With Unclear Mineral Language
paragraphs: A lot of early-to-mid-century deeds in this area are ambiguous about whether mineral rights transferred along with the surface, particularly when the sale was informal or handled without an attorney. We read the actual language on your family's deed rather than assuming based on how the transaction is usually remembered.

faqs.question: Our family's roots are in Prichard, but the land in question is somewhere else in the county. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes, we research wherever the actual tract sits, not where the family currently lives.

faqs.question: The old deed doesn't clearly say whether minerals were included in the sale. What now?
faqs.answer: We read the specific language and, where it's genuinely ambiguous, explain what that means for your family's claim before we make an offer.

faqs.question: Is there oil and gas activity anywhere near Prichard itself?
faqs.answer: Little directly under the city, but plenty of Prichard families hold interests in the more rural parts of Mobile County. We check each specific tract.

faqs.question: Our family has more than one heir with a claim to the same old interest. Can you still work with us?
faqs.answer: Yes. We identify every heir of record and can structure a purchase that lets each co-owner sell their own share, together or separately.

faqs.question: How long does it usually take to confirm an interest like this?
faqs.answer: It depends on how many transfers the land has been through, but most Prichard-area interests take one to three weeks to fully trace.
